Sorry, #831 got the fix wrong. Computer use isn't a server tool: the model returns `computer_call`, the app performs the action and sends a screenshot back as `computer_call_output` on the next request, the same loop as `function_call` / `function_call_output`. So it should be recorded as a client `ToolCall` with `finish_reason="tool_call"`, not as a `ServerToolCallPart` with `stop`.

It's skipped today only because `_is_tool_call_item` / `_tool_call_arguments` expect `name` + `arguments`/`input`, and `computer_call` has neither. Something along these lines in `get_output_messages_from_response`, reusing the existing absorb/append logic:

```python
def _computer_call_to_tool_call(item: ResponseComputerToolCall) -> ToolCall:
    return ToolCall(
        id=item.call_id,
        name="computer",
        # newer SDKs batch actions into `actions`; older ones send a single `action`
        arguments=item.model_dump(
            include={"action", "actions"}, exclude_none=True, mode="json"
        ),
    )
```

`extract_finish_reasons` would need to count it as `tool_calls` as well.

`computer_call_output` is an input item the app sends on the next request, so `responses.create` won't return it in `output`. It probably belongs in `_get_input_message` as a `ToolCallResponsePart`, with the replayed `computer_call` input item recorded as a `ToolCall`:

```python
_TOOL_OUTPUT_TYPES = frozenset(
    {"function_call_output", "custom_tool_call_output", "computer_call_output"}
)
```

(plus a `computer_call` branch next to `_TOOL_CALL_ARGUMENT_FIELDS` that uses `action`/`actions` as the arguments).

These tests feed hand-built payloads to the extractor, so they confirm the mapping we chose rather than what the API actually does, which is how the client/server mix-up got through. Could you replace them with a multi-turn VCR test in `test_responses.py` (sync + async), next to `test_responses_create_captures_custom_tool_history`? Turn 1 gets a real `computer_call`, turn 2 replays it and sends the screenshot back using the SDK input types:

```python
from openai.types.responses import ResponseComputerToolCall
from openai.types.responses.response_input_item_param import ComputerCallOutput

COMPUTER_TOOL = {
    "type": "computer_use_preview",
    "display_width": 1024,
    "display_height": 768,
    "environment": "browser",
}


@pytest.mark.vcr()
def test_responses_create_captures_computer_call_loop(
    request, span_exporter, openai_client, instrument_with_content
):
    _skip_if_not_latest()

    history = [{"role": "user", "content": "Open bing.com"}]
    first = openai_client.responses.create(
        model="computer-use-preview",
        tools=[COMPUTER_TOOL],
        input=history,
        truncation="auto",
    )
    (computer_call,) = [
        item for item in first.output if isinstance(item, ResponseComputerToolCall)
    ]

    openai_client.responses.create(
        model="computer-use-preview",
        tools=[COMPUTER_TOOL],
        truncation="auto",
        input=[
            *history,
            *first.output,
            ComputerCallOutput(
                type="computer_call_output",
                call_id=computer_call.call_id,
                output={"type": "computer_screenshot", "image_url": SCREENSHOT_DATA_URL},
            ),
        ],
    )

    first_span, second_span = span_exporter.get_finished_spans()

    assert first_span.attributes[GenAIAttributes.GEN_AI_RESPONSE_FINISH_REASONS] == ("tool_calls",)
    output_messages = _load_span_messages(first_span, GenAIAttributes.GEN_AI_OUTPUT_MESSAGES)
    (tool_call,) = [
        p for m in output_messages for p in m["parts"] if p["type"] == "tool_call"
    ]
    assert tool_call["name"] == "computer"
    assert tool_call["id"] == computer_call.call_id
    assert isinstance(tool_call["arguments"], dict)

    input_messages = _load_span_messages(second_span, GenAIAttributes.GEN_AI_INPUT_MESSAGES)
    input_parts = [p for m in input_messages for p in m["parts"]]
    (replayed_call,) = [p for p in input_parts if p["type"] == "tool_call"]
    (tool_response,) = [p for p in input_parts if p["type"] == "tool_call_response"]
    assert replayed_call["name"] == "computer"
    assert replayed_call["id"] == tool_response["id"] == computer_call.call_id
    assert input_messages[-1]["role"] == "tool"
```

If you don't have access to the computer-use model, it's fine to have AI generate the cassette from the documented response shape, just start it with `# TODO: this is generated by AI, re-record` so it gets re-recorded later.
